pending_evidence_review.rule: Continue unconsidered pending evidence in canon/native order. Revisit an already considered uncertainty only when a substantive new passage lead can be checked. This cursor never starts New Testament source review.

completion_definition: Completed means the initial curated cross-reference pass: the source verse and every listed target passage were read in the pinned Saints-Translation English records, and each retained pair has a specific explanation. It does not mean every possible biblical connection has been exhausted, or independent scholarly approval.

unresolved_candidates.reason: Both authorities are amazed, but the young man is admired for disregarding bodily pains, whereas the council marvels at the boldness of unlettered Peter and John. target_units.text: When they observed Peter’s and John’s boldness and realized that they were unlettered, ordinary men, they were amazed. They also recognized that they had been with Jesus.
Seeing the man who had been healed standing with them, they had nothing to say against it.
They ordered them to leave the council and conferred with one another,
saying, “What should we do with these men? That a notable sign has taken place through them is evident to everyone living in Jerusalem, and we cannot deny it.
But so that it spreads no further among the people, let us warn them with threats not to speak to anyone in this name again.”
They called them in and ordered them neither to speak nor to teach at all in the name of Jesus.
Peter and John answered them, “Judge whether it is right before God to listen to you rather than to God;
for we cannot keep from speaking about what we have seen and heard.”
After further threats, they released them, finding no way to punish them because of the people, since everyone was glorifying God for what had happened.

unresolved_candidates.source_text: Let him not trust that he will endure, for empty things will result for him.
unresolved_candidates.reason: Eliphaz warns the ungodly person not to trust that he will endure, while Psalms 61:10-11 addresses human vanity, injustice, plunder and attachment to wealth. The proposed link depends on supplying wealth as the object of trust in this source sentence; that broad association is not retained as a particular match.

target_units.text: Nevertheless the sons of men are vain; the sons of men are false upon scales for doing injustice, they themselves together from vanity.

unresolved_candidates.source_text: They unjustly lay in ambush in narrow places and did not know a righteous road.
unresolved_candidates.reason: Job explicitly describes an unjust ambush in narrow places and ignorance of a righteous road. The native Proverbs text instead describes hiding a righteous man in the earth, seizing his property, and refusing the criminals' paths. It was not rewritten as an ambush proposal; the general violent-path association alone was not retained.

target_units.text: Come with us; share in bloodshed. Let us hide a righteous man in the earth unjustly;
let us swallow him alive like Hades and remove his memory from the earth.
Let us seize his costly property and fill our houses with spoils.
Cast your lot among us; let us all obtain a common purse, and let there be one moneybag for us.
Do not walk in the way with them; turn your foot away from their paths,
for their feet run toward evil, and they are quick to shed blood.

unresolved_candidates.source_text: The abyss said, ‘It is not in me,’ and the sea said, ‘It is not with me.’
unresolved_candidates.reason: The sea in Job denies that wisdom is with it. Deuteronomy says its command is not across the sea and is instead near the hearer. These concern different spatial claims and different subjects; shared sea imagery and the general question of instruction were not sufficient to retain a pair.

target_units.text: For this commandment which I command you this day is not excessively burdensome, neither is it far from you.
It is not in heaven above, that you should say, Who shall ascend for us into heaven, and fetch it for us, that we may hear it and do it?
Neither is it beyond the sea, that you should say, Who shall cross for us unto the other side of the sea, and fetch it for us, and make us hear it, that we may do it?
The word is very near you, in your mouth, and in your heart, and in your hands, that you may do it.
